name: Hull
metaTitle: Best Soft Play in Hull 2026 | Indoor Play Centres for Parents
metaDescription: Find the best soft play in Hull. Our 2026 guide covers indoor play centres across Hull and East Riding — with prices, facilities, SEN sessions, and tips for parents.
intro:
Hull parents know the drill — horizontal rain off the Humber and a three-year-old who's already lapped the living room twice. Soft play in Hull isn't a luxury, it's survival. The good news is that Hull and the surrounding East Riding have a solid spread of indoor play centres, from budget community spots in Bransholme to larger commercial venues out toward Hessle and Kingswood. Whether you've got a crawling baby or a boisterous eight-year-old, there's something here for you.

Hull's indoor play scene suits all ages and budgets. You'll find everything from calm, toddler-only venues with padded floors and sensory corners to multi-level adventure frames with ball cannons, rope bridges, and zip lines for older children. Most venues also have on-site cafes — the quality of the coffee varies wildly, so it's worth checking before you commit to a long session. The better venues separate age groups into distinct zones, which makes a real difference if you're bringing a crawling baby alongside an older sibling.

Prices for soft play in Hull are good value compared to cities like Leeds or Sheffield, typically ranging from £4 to £9 per child for a standard session. Under-1s are free at most venues. Off-peak weekday sessions are noticeably cheaper and quieter — Tuesday to Thursday mornings between 9am and 11am are the sweet spot for anyone wanting a calmer experience. Weekend slots fill fast, so book online in advance where possible. Most larger Hull venues now run timed sessions rather than open-ended play, so check before you arrive.

If you need [SEN-friendly soft play in Hull](/soft-play/hull/sen-friendly), several venues run dedicated quiet sessions with reduced lighting, no music, and capped numbers. These book up quickly — following venues on social media is the best way to catch availability. For [birthday parties in Hull](/soft-play/hull/birthday-parties), the larger venues around Kingswood and east Hull offer full packages from around £120 upwards, including a dedicated host and party room. Book at least six weeks ahead for a Saturday slot — they go fast.

Hull's soft play venues are spread across the city, so there's usually something within easy reach wherever you're based — from Anlaby and Hessle in the west to Holderness Road in the east, and north into Bransholme and Kingswood. Families in the East Riding can also find options nearby in [Beverley](/soft-play/beverley) and [Bridlington](/soft-play/bridlington). Our directory covers the wider area so you can find indoor play near Hull wherever you are in East Yorkshire.

faqs.question: What age do children need to be for soft play in Hull?
faqs.answer: Most soft play centres in Hull welcome children from around 6 months, with dedicated baby and toddler zones for under-3s. Age limits vary by venue — larger frame venues typically cap at 11 or 12 years. Always check the venue's website before visiting.

faqs.question: How much does soft play cost in Hull?
faqs.answer: Soft play in Hull typically costs £4–£9 per child for a standard session. Under-1s are free at most venues. Toddlers (1–3) tend to pay £4–£6, while children aged 3–12 pay £5.50–£9. Off-peak weekday sessions are usually cheaper. Birthday party packages start from around £120 depending on venue and guest numbers.

faqs.question: Do adults have to pay entry at Hull soft play centres?
faqs.answer: At most Hull soft play venues, accompanying adults enter free — though some charge a small fee of £1–£3, or ask adults to purchase food or drink from the café. Wacky Warehouse venues typically require adults to buy something from the pub. Always check before you go.

faqs.question: Are there SEN-friendly soft play options in Hull?
faqs.answer: Yes. Several Hull soft play venues run dedicated SEN sessions with reduced lighting, no music, and capped numbers. These sessions book up quickly — follow venues on Facebook and check individual venue pages for the latest times. Our SEN filter shows all venues with inclusive provision.

faqs.question: What's the best soft play in Hull for a birthday party?
faqs.answer: The larger venues in Kingswood and east Hull consistently get strong reviews for birthday party packages — look for venues offering a dedicated party host, food packages, and a reserved party room. Book at least 4–6 weeks ahead for weekend slots, as they fill up fast.

faqs.question: Is there free parking at Hull soft play centres?
faqs.answer: Most Hull soft play venues on the outskirts of the city — particularly those in Kingswood, Bransholme, Hessle, and retail park locations — offer free on-site parking. City-centre and inner-city venues on routes like Beverley Road and Spring Bank may require street parking or nearby pay-and-display.

faqs.question: When is the best time to visit soft play in Hull?
faqs.answer: The quietest times at Hull soft play centres are weekday mornings, particularly Tuesday to Thursday between 9am and 11am. Weekends and school holidays are the busiest periods. If you need a calmer environment — especially for younger children or those with additional needs — mid-week mornings are the best bet.

faqs.question: What should I bring to soft play in Hull?
faqs.answer: Socks are required at every Hull soft play venue — grip socks are ideal. Bring a spare change of clothes for younger children, a water bottle, and any snacks if the venue allows outside food (most have cafés). Baby-changing facilities are available at the majority of venues. Keep valuables in the car where possible.
